title: Power Pages: client APIs for scripting forms, lists, users and data
summary: Hold: Microsoft documents Web API column configuration applying to $pages.webAPI calls, so the briefing should not leave that control's applicability unresolved. The anonymous-access warning also needs a tenant-control qualification, and two controls named in the checklist are missing from the controls table.

claims.claim: Power Pages enforces table permissions on the server and the client API cannot override them.
claims.quote: Power Pages applies form metadata and table permissions on the server, and the client API can't override those settings.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance: Before rollout; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Associated web roles and table permissions bound the records and operations available to site Web API calls.
claims.quote: The portal Web API accesses table (entity) records and follows the table permissions given to users through the associated [web role](../security/create-web-roles).

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Granting the Anonymous users web role table access makes the table's data available to any visitor.
claims.quote: When the Anonymous users web role is granted access to a table, any user who visits the site can access the data in the table.
claims.fix: Also cite https://learn.microsoft.com/power-pages/security/disable-anonymous-access and qualify the warning: the tenant's Anonymous access to Dataverse control can override maker table permissions and block anonymous reads, while anonymous writes can remain possible.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: setVisible(false) hides a form control in the browser rather than securing its data.
claims.quote: The `setVisible(false)` method hides a control in the browser only. Use table permissions and column security to protect data. Never rely on hiding a control to secure data.

claims.claim: row.setVisible(false) changes only the presentation of a list row.
claims.quote: Hiding a row changes only what people see in the list; it doesn't change the data or the number of records that the server returns.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft instructs developers to protect data with table permissions and column security rather than presentation methods.
claims.quote: Use table permissions and column security to protect data. Never rely on hiding a control to secure data.

claims.claim: The client API authentication reference gives no method to change accepted identity providers.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages client API identity providers. Opened client-api/user-authentication in full; its only methods are signIn and signOut, neither of which configures identity providers.

claims.claim: $pages.ajax.request automatically adds the CSRF token to every request.
claims.quote: **Cross-site request forgery (CSRF) token**: The token is retrieved when it's first needed, cached in memory, and added to the header of every request.

claims.claim: $pages.ajax requests include the visitor's session cookie.
claims.quote: **Credentials**: The session cookie is included with every request.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; controls[1].note; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft Learn does not establish whether Web API table and column site settings apply to $pages.webAPI.
claims.quote:
Common call patterns include:

```javascript
$.ajax(...)
fetch(...)
webapi.safeAjax(...)
$pages.webAPI.retrieveRecord(...)
$pages.webAPI.retrieveMultipleRecords(...)
```
claims.fix: Cite this troubleshooting page: it explicitly includes $pages.webAPI calls in Web API column-configuration migration and tells readers to verify Webapi/<table-name>/enabled=True. Replace the unresolved-applicability statements with that documented relationship. Explain that fields uses explicit columns, optionally combined with UseFieldsFromView on supported versions; wildcard fields are no longer supported. Remove the corresponding open question. The narrower observation that the client API reference itself omits these settings can remain only alongside this documentation.

claims.claim: The client agent API checks the current user's access to the agent.
claims.quote: Use the Power Pages Client API `$pages.agent` object and its SendActivity method to send messages or invoke events in the Microsoft Copilot Studio agent available to the current user.

claims.claim: getRecordCount returns at most 5,000.
claims.quote: The server returns a maximum count of 5,000. When a table contains more than 5,000 records, the result is 5,000.

claims.claim: Learn recommends retrieveMultipleRecords with $count=true to retrieve records with their total in @odata.count.
claims.quote: That method returns the collection in the `value` property of the response, and the total count in the `@odata.count` property.

claims.quote: Portals Web API operations require a Power Pages license.

claims.claim: The portals Web API overview says authenticated calls need the applicable authenticated user capacity licences.

claims.where: Governance guidance: At rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: The checklist's instruction to enforce rules through column security is represented in the controls table.
claims.quote: The checklist says 'enforce rules through table permissions and column security'; the table contains table permissions, portals Web API site settings and a client API switch gap, but no column-security row.
claims.fix: Add a separate column-security control row, or remove column security from the actionable checklist while retaining the sourced explanation in Risk assessment. Research its exact UI and automation routes before populating that row.

claims.where: Governance guidance: At rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: The checklist's cloud-flow registration and web-role control is represented in the controls table.
claims.quote: The checklist says 'Confirm that any cloud flow a script triggers is registered with the site and secured with a web role'; none of the three control rows covers cloud-flow registration or access.
claims.fix: Add a site-scoped cloud-flow registration/access row. UI: Power Pages > site > + Edit > Set up > Integrations > Cloud flows > + Add cloud flow > select flow > Roles > + Add roles > select roles > Save. Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/power-pages/configure/cloud-flow-integration and research automation before filling that side or marking it undocumented.
